questions.extractedQuestion: Let P be the set of all triangles in a plane and R be the relation defined on P as aRb if a is similar to b. Prove that R is an equivalence relation.
steps: Two triangles are similar when their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides have a common positive scale factor.
Reflexive: every triangle has the same angles and side lengths as itself; scale factor 1, so aRa.
Symmetric: if triangle a is similar to b with scale factor k>0, the reverse correspondence has scale factor 1/k>0, so bRa.
Transitive: if a is similar to b with scale factor k>0 and b is similar to c with scale factor h>0, corresponding angles remain equal and the composed scale factor kh>0, so aRc.
Thus similarity is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; R is an equivalence relation.
